title: The Smallest Door
thesis: The federal government did not cut Alaska Native funding. It raised the floor. The smallest award an Alaska applicant could win in this lane went from one hundred thousand dollars to two and a half million, and the field went from Alaska only to nationwide, and the thing that big new award is paid to produce is a list that a much smaller grant in Anchorage already produced for free.
long_form: On July 28th the Administration for Native Americans published a final notice retiring SEDS and SEDS Alaska. Its successor, EAGLE, is bigger: twenty four million dollars and thirty one awards against SEDS Alaska's two million and three. In the same notice ANA created the AI3 Action Institute, one award, nationwide, with a floor of two and a half million dollars, whose job is to identify responsible and practical opportunities to apply AI in Native communities. Nobody has been cut and nobody has been denied. What changed is the size of the smallest door. SEDS Alaska's floor was one hundred thousand dollars, which is a sum a village office can administer, and its field was Alaska. AI3's floor is two and a half million, and its field is every federally recognized tribe plus Native CDFIs, Urban Indian Centers, Tribal Colleges and Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander serving agencies. Meanwhile a three hundred and eighty thousand dollar NSF grant to the University of Alaska Anchorage asked any Alaskan organization to name its own problem. Twelve wrote one down. Four were funded, among them Nome Joint Utilities System on predicting the thermal conductivity of warming permafrost, and the Village of Alakanuk Tribe on AI for rural community transformation and infrastructure coordination. That set of twelve is the deliverable AI3 is being paid to produce, and it already exists for Alaska.
valence: curious and wary, unresolved, with a live deadline
valence_defense: Alarm is unavailable on the facts. Nobody has been denied anything, no AI3 award has been made, no EAGLE award is announced, and the successor program carries more money and more awards than the program it succeeded. Celebration is unavailable too, because a bigger pot arranged as one national award is a different instrument, and the Alaska alternative has published no results at all. The honest posture is a structural observation and a deadline fifteen days out.
falsifiability: FALSE if ANA posts an FY2026 Alaska specific competition, or if an EAGLE or IDEAS award floor lands at or below nine hundred thousand dollars with an open project definition, or if the AI3 award announced after August 27th 2026 goes to a Native led applicant that runs its own open call for community named problems. Any one of those and the thesis is wrong.
supporting_facts: SEDS Alaska FY2025: two million dollars, three awards, floor one hundred thousand, ceiling nine hundred thousand, closed July 22nd 2025. For FY2026 grants.gov returns three ANA opportunities and none is Alaska specific.
AI3 Action Institute: one award, nationwide, floor two and a half million dollars, ceiling and total program funding both three and a half million, closes August 27th 2026.
NSF award 2433241 to UAA, three hundred and eighty thousand dollars. Its mini grant call was open to any Alaskan organization outside the university. Twelve asked, four were funded.
fair_counterpoint_that_gets_a_scene: Consolidation is a rational answer to a real problem, and Act 3 gives it the widest, best lit scene in the film. Two hundred and twenty nine federally recognized tribes in Alaska, and five hundred and seventy five federally recognized entities nationwide, each separately evaluating the same vendors and each separately failing to negotiate data sovereignty terms, is a worse outcome than one body doing it once. Vendor leverage, shared governance language and a reusable sovereignty framework are exactly the goods a one hundred thousand dollar village award can never buy. EAGLE is also genuinely larger than what it succeeded. ANA ran a real process: a proposed notice on March 20th, a thirty day comment period, thirty two submissions, and it widened Welders to Elders past welding in response to comment. And ANA wrote that Alaska Native communities remain eligible across EAGLE project areas including IDEAS, a project area whose name is Indigenous Designs to Empower and Advance Self Determination.
how_it_narrows_honestly: The film does not say the institute is a mistake, because it is not. It says the institute and the retirement of the small Alaska lane arrived in one package, and only the second of those is the problem. It grades design against design and says out loud that neither side has published a result, and that AI3 has no grantee at all until after August 27th.
the_lazy_angle_we_refuse: Two, one on each side. We refuse the feds killed Alaska Native funding and swapped it for an AI buzzword, which is false: Alaska Native villages are explicitly eligible, the successor program is larger, and no application has been rejected. We refuse its mirror, a twenty seven and a half million dollar AI windfall, because most of that is EAGLE and not AI, and one national award is a windfall for nobody who does not win it.
who_it_serves: An Alaska Native village council, tribal consortium, Native CDFI or Tribal College with a decision to make in fifteen days: lead a bid by August 27th, join somebody else's as a named partner, or compete under EAGLE instead. And any Alaska organization that had a problem SEDS Alaska would have funded, who now needs to know where the remaining small door is.
throughline_object: THE SILL, the award floor drawn as a physical threshold you must step over, whose height changes when the rule changes

runners_up.angle: AI3 replaced Alaska's grant program with an AI institute
runners_up.why_it_lost: REFUTED BY THE PRIMARY DOCUMENT. ANA writes that the Institute will complement, not replace, broader social and economic development efforts. EAGLE is the successor. The fact check killed this framing before it reached a script.

runners_up.angle: The federal government told Native communities what their problems are while Alaska let them name their own
runners_up.why_it_lost: The red team killed it on four counts. EAGLE contains IDEAS, an explicitly open self determination project area, so the menu is not closed. UAA also gatekept, twelve in and four out, picked by a university committee with a faculty PI on every funded project. RAISE is an NSF capacity grant open to any Alaskan organization with no Native mandate, so the Native self determination frame was imported rather than found. And RAISE began in August 2024, so it is not an answer to a July 2026 rule and the ten days apart framing manufactured a dialogue that never happened.

runners_up.angle: The AI learning curve the institute targets has already closed inside Alaska's tribal health system
runners_up.why_it_lost: The evidence is one symposium report whose authors describe their own 2025 group as a homogenous group of individuals working with electronic health record data, thirty one people, at least sixteen percent of them from Stanford and the CDC. It says nothing about communities and nothing about ANA. Carrying it would have cost six binding narrowings for a point the spine does not need. Cut whole.

cultural_ruling_binding: The subject is federal program design and public documents. The film never describes what Alaska Native people want, need, fear or lost.
No Alaska Federation of Natives position may appear. Its only source is a confirmed HTTP 403 and AFN's own reachable site carries no statement on this.

The film states on screen that no Alaska Native political or advocacy organization was reachable for a position, so it speaks about the program and not for anyone affected by it, and it invites correction.
Every position traces to 91 FR 47241, a grants.gov notice, the NSF award record or the funder's own page, or is owned as this publisher's opinion.
Never say Alakanuk, Nome Joint Utilities System or any partner named its own problem, endorses this framing or holds any view. The call invited it and they are the named partners. That is all.
Federally recognized tribes, ANCSA village and regional corporations, nonprofit tribal consortia, tribal health organizations and advocacy bodies are legally distinct and none speaks for the others.
32 submissions is a total comment count. Not 32 Alaskans, not 32 objections. Nothing in the record states how many objected.

NEVER draw with a face: any Alaska Native person or community, any tribe or tribal government, any real named organization or person, villages, medevac aircraft, or any mask, totemic or Indigenous visual form. No Indigenous motif is used decoratively anywhere.
Characterization is permitted ONLY for paperwork and programs: the notice, the funding line, the sill, the slips, the queue.
